title: Session micro-shard prefix folding and KV optimizer for cross-request reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We propose a new runtime sub-system called 'session micro-shard prefix folding' (SMPF) to increase cross-request KV cache reuse while minimizing GPU memory pressure and contention during continuous batching. SMPF differs from prior prefix dedupe work by actively folding similar prefix fragments across short time windows into compact micro-shards that are GPU-resident and reference-counted, enabling multi-request reuse without duplicating KV state per slab.

Problem statement:
- High-frequency small prompts (chat-like interactions) create many overlapping prefix fragments; naive per-request KV writes replicate tensors and blow GPU memory.
- Current dedupe approaches handle exact-match fingerprints but struggle with near-duplicates, partial overlaps, and interleaved batching.
- Locking and eviction at slab granularity cause stalls in continuous batching pipelines, increasing tail latency.

Design overview:
1) Signature generation: compute a compact locality-preserving signature for each prefix fragment (64-bit rolling hash + content-length bucket + model-arch tag). Signatures are cheap and compatible with LSH sketching.
2) Micro-shard formation: a background worker aggregates signatures within a 2s sliding window and forms micro-shards (small contiguous KV chunks) by coalescing fragments with high similarity (LSH threshold). Micro-shards are content-addressed and stored in a GPU-resident coalesced slab region.
3) Fold-on-reference: new requests map their prefixes to micro-shard signatures. When an overlap exists, request execution uses a lightweight indirection (micro-shard ref) instead of copying KV tensors into a per-request slab.
4) Eviction and refcounting: micro-shards maintain strong refcounts per-GPU; an async epoch-based reclamation reduces locking in the hot path. Aging policy prioritizes micro-shards with high per-token reuse and low mutation frequency.
5) Partial overlap handling: for fragment overlaps that are not full-contained, SMPF supports delta stitching: retrieve the shared micro-shard and append small per-request deltas kept in a transient LRU that lives in host memory and is promoted to GPU only when needed.
6) Integration with continuous batching: during batch formation we expose micro-shard hints so the scheduler can co-locate requests that share shards on the same GPU to avoid cross-device transfers and copying. For multi-GPU pools, SMPF supports affinity hints and a best-effort co-scheduling window to improve reuse without stalling batching.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs CPU: sketching and background coalescing require CPU cycles but reduce GPU resident memory. We expect net cost savings for typical chat workloads because GPU memory is the scarce resource.
- Consistency vs latency: epoch reclamation avoids synchronous locks on hot path but can allow short-lived stale refs; acceptable because KV is read-only during generation.
- Near-duplication coverage: LSH thresholds control sensitivity; lower thresholds increase reuse but risk incorrect merging of dissimilar fragments (we set conservative defaults and provide tuning knobs).

Metrics and targets:
- Primary metrics: micro-shard hit-rate, GPU KV resident bytes saved, per-request token cost, p50/p95 generation latency, batch formation wait time.
- Targets for rollout canary: 12%+ token cost reduction on chat-heavy traffic, <3% increase in batch wait time, p95 latency within 5% of baseline.

Experiments so far (internal results):
- Synthetic chat mix (60% short prompts, 40% long): micro-shard prototype reduced peak GPU KV footprint by 18% and end-to-end token cost by 9% in our lab run.
- Mixed-tenant stress run: colocating shard-sharing requests decreased cross-GPU memcpy by 24% and improved throughput by ~6% under 90th percentile load.
- Edge case: highly-unique single-turn requests saw no improvement and minor host CPU overhead (+3%), which is acceptable with feature flag disabled.

Implementation plan (high level tasks):
- T1: Signature & LSH sketching library (Rust) + unit tests.
- T2: Micro-shard store abstraction (GPU-resident allocator hooks + content-addressing).
- T3: Background coalescer worker and sliding-window aggregator service.
- T4: Integration into batching scheduler to emit affinity hints.
- T5: Epoch-based reclamation and refcounting; host transient delta LRU.
- T6: Telemetry and dashboards (new metrics, p95 tracking, memory heatmaps).
- T7: Canary rollout with feature flag and A/B harness.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration shows >=10% token cost reduction for target workload in canary.
- No regression >5% in p95 generation latency for non-sharing workloads.
- Telemetry dashboards and alerts added before 10% rollout.
- Implementation covered by unit and integration tests; code review + security review completed.

Rollout plan:
- Start with canary on Dedicated pools with synthetic workflows (5% traffic), monitor for 72h.
- Expand to 20% after confirming metrics and no memory leak.
- Full rollout subject to performance gate and security review.

- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.internal/confluence/runtime/smpf-design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1458
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood/runtime/smpf-experiments
- Safety/arch review notes: https://redwood.internal/docs/arch/reviews/smpf

Related tickets / dependencies:
- ENG-31245 (probabilistic-prefix-compaction) - synergy on compaction heuristics
- ENG-61234 (prefix-atlas compact slab allocator) - allocator hooks required
- ENG-70321 (opportunistic-prefix-clustering) - sampling algorithms to share

Open risks and mitigation:
- Risk: micro-shard refcount churn increases CPU overhead under extreme churn. Mitigation: adaptive coalescing window, backpressure to disable SMPF in hot churn windows.
- Risk: rare merge collisions from LSH false positives. Mitigation: conservative threshold + verification pass during shard finalization.

Next steps (this week):
- Complete signature library (T1) and land prototype benchmark harness.
- Schedule 1-hour sync with Allocator and Batching owners to align on hooks (invite: @Marcel, @Chen).
